f76585a8f3eb568e:en: The Islamabad Memorandum (a 60-day time-limited agreement) signed on June 17 at the Palace of Versailles expired on August 17. Iran refused an extension, and President Trump threatened to bomb even Oman, the mediating country, saying "raise the white flag." On August 19, an ultra-strong sanctions campaign named 'Economic D-Day' was announced, and on the same day, the UAE indefinitely suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Airstrikes on Iranian territory have been halted for over three weeks since July 29, and Iran's missile and drone launches are effectively at zero. Instead, dual blockades (the US Navy's blockade of Iranian ports + Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz) and attacks on merchant ships have taken the place of war, with southern Lebanon being the only front where gunfire is still exchanged.

9a5a5b8347243c00:en: Since this is an ongoing war, nearly every figure has variations depending on the party reporting it. Iranian military death tolls differ 2 to 5 times between US/Israeli claims (over 6,000) and Iranian/independent tallies (1,221~3,636), and US war costs differ 3-fold between the official $37.5 billion and independent estimates exceeding $100 billion. Below, we have noted "who claimed the figure" wherever possible, and content claimed by only one side and unverified has been marked separately. A list of conflicting figures has been compiled separately in the final chapter.
e271747e2c78c76a:en: • Why it happened. On top of the structural hostility since the 1979 revolution, diplomacy was blocked by the 2018 collapse of the nuclear deal, and as the 'Axis of Resistance' crumbled between 2023 and 2025, Iran's deterrence disappeared. On top of this, the large-scale anti-government protests that began in December 2025 planted the calculation in Washington and Jerusalem that "the regime could be toppled now."
a404b631399592fc:en: • How it started. In February 2026, in Oman and Geneva, a deal seemed imminent as Iran proposed "zero enriched uranium stockpile + full IAEA verification," but just two days later, in the early morning of February 28, the US and Israel launched a surprise attack. The Supreme Leader was eliminated on the first day.
ecaa0bfff8ef6df4:en: • How it unfolded. Iran's missile launch rate dropped by over 90% within ten days, but it held out with the asymmetric card of closing the Strait of Hormuz. As the passage through which one-fifth of the world's oil flows was blocked, the war shifted from a military issue to a global economic issue.
7355d0bb6d769fe1:en: • What is blocked right now. ① Strait sovereignty ② US Navy blockade ③ war reparations ④ order of sanctions relief ⑤ enrichment rights ⑥ Lebanon — these six are entangled in a structure where none can be resolved first.
3a325f4b087ac751:en: • Why does it matter to Korea? 70.7% of crude oil, 20.4% of LNG, and 34.4% of naphtha come from the Middle East. Korea was one of four countries that received force majeure notices when Qatar's LNG facility was struck in March, and by August, joint Korea-US military exercises were even scaled back as a consequence of refusing to support Iran operations.
835217330a3429cf:en: This war did not suddenly arise in 2026. Twelve strata have piled up, and in each stratum a safety pin has come loose. The reason this part is the longest in this document is that almost everything that happened in 2026 has its origin here.
b2fa5ce73d4ff135:en: Oil and Sovereignty — Every Iran Crisis Has an Oil Clause
2d17f36a5def4bba:en: A single contract signed in 1901 created every conflict in modern Iranian history. The basic emotion Iranians feel when looking at foreign powers — "foreigners are taking what is ours" — began here.
b7392a8b007359e1:en: • In 1901, the Englishman William Knox D'Arcy obtained a 60-year oil concession over most of Persia. In exchange, he paid 20,000 pounds in cash, 20,000 pounds in shares, and 16% of future net profits.
ce06a0323d45c76f:en: • On May 26, 1908, the Middle East's first commercial oil field was discovered at Masjed Soleyman. In 1909 the Anglo-Persian Oil Company (APOC) was established, and in 1914, First Lord of the Admiralty Churchill purchased a 51% stake on behalf of the British government. From that moment, Iran's oil became fuel for the British Navy.
da385842fff8c957:en: • The core dispute lay in the phrase "16% of net profits." Iran had no access to APOC's accounts, and the structure was such that the taxes the British government collected from APOC exceeded the royalties Iran received.
8ffe0de4f148b5fa:en: The Constitutional Revolution — Ancestor of Today's Guardian Council
9ac57763ea4a03c0:en: That same year, the Anglo-Russian Convention divided Iran into a northern (Russian) zone, a southern (British) zone, and a neutral zone without Iran's participation, and in 1908 a Cossack Brigade led by a Russian officer shelled the parliament. In 1911, a Russian ultimatum led to the dissolution of parliament, ending the revolution. It was at this point that the experience of "great powers dividing us over our heads" became engraved in memory.
ee400e8474915cd6:en: Reza Shah — The Archetype of Modernization and Backlash
e078707c31091ee5:en: Reza Shah canceled the D'Arcy concession in 1932, but the new 1933 agreement, while slightly improving terms, extended the concession period to 1993, which was in fact received in Iran as a defeat. In 1941, Britain and the Soviet Union invaded Iran (over the issue of German technicians and to secure a supply route to the USSR), and he abdicated and died in South Africa.
8eec8c603432eed9:en:
1951.03

Parliament votes almost unanimously to nationalize oil. In April, Mohammad Mosaddegh becomes prime minister and the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) is established.
cf3bfd24a958eb66:en:
1951.10

Britain withdraws from the world's largest refinery at Abadan, and the British Navy enforces a global embargo on Iranian oil. Iran's oil revenue effectively collapses to zero between 1951 and 1953.
6d0d1fe95dbb0b36:en:
1952.07

Britain loses at both the International Court of Justice and the UN Security Council. The Truman administration refuses to participate in a coup.
6392fab5b4507ce8:en:
1953.08.19

After Eisenhower takes office, the US reverses its position and carries out the CIA's Operation TPAJAX / MI6's Operation Boot. Kermit Roosevelt directs the operation on the ground, and paid crowds along with the forces of General Fazlollah Zahedi seize control of Tehran. The death toll was 200–300 (some estimates say 800 — disputed).
539304906102aa0e:en:
1954

Consortium Agreement: BP (formerly AIOC) 40%, five major American companies 40%, Shell 14%, France's CFP 6%. Britain's monopoly ended, but so did Iran's control.
69b9840b169e296b:en:
2013.08.19

The US National Security Archive releases internal CIA records — officially confirming for the first time that the coup was "carried out under CIA direction" as "an act of US foreign policy conceived and approved at the highest levels".
a56a995fcea4bc7d:en: Known in the Iranian calendar as '28 Mordad', this incident is the genesis of Iranian anti-Americanism. Before this, unlike Britain and Russia, the United States was seen by Iranians as a friendly third party without a history of imperialism. After 1953, the United States became the guarantor of dictatorship. The Islamic Republic still repeatedly cites this incident today, and the direct motive behind the 1979 seizure of the US embassy was also the fear that "the US would repeat 1953 again."
9d5c9d00054639f6:en: The Pahlavi Regime and Revolution — Collapse Built by Oil
2be5263387f12486:en: Founded in 1957 with CIA support, and joined by Mossad in training from 1960, this was the secret police. In scale, the organization itself claimed fewer than 2,000 members, while historians estimate 4,000 to 6,000 full-time staff backed by a vast network of informants (the postrevolutionary claim of 15,000 has not been verified). Electric shock torture, flogging, and beatings are documented, and in 1976 Amnesty International rated Iran's human rights record among the worst in the world. What SAVAK actually accomplished was annihilating the secular opposition — the National Front (liberal), the Tudeh Party (communist), and the Fedayeen and MEK (guerrilla groups) were all destroyed, and the mosque remained the only space the state could not fully control. This explains why the clergy took over the revolution in 1979.
be2f2c9a9d7b2b22:en: The White Revolution — A Failure Born of Success
0bd2d8f22a171883:en: • Reforms in six points (later expanded to nineteen) beginning in January of 1963: land reform, nationalization of forests, sale of state enterprises, worker profit-sharing, women's suffrage, and the Literacy Corps.
d5c69767240abd42:en: • The achievements were real — land was redistributed to about 2.5 million households, nearly 90% of tenant farmers became landowners on paper (affecting roughly 40% of the population), and the literacy rate rose from 26% to 42%.
95546e680656660f:en: • However, most of the distributed land was too small to be self-sufficient, and credit and irrigation support were lacking. The result was the destruction of rural social order and mass migration to the cities — the slums of southern Tehran expanded, and these people became the foot soldiers of the 1979 revolution.
eab1849635a04978:en: • For the clergy, this was a triple blow. Land reform eroded religious endowments (waqf), women's suffrage and non-Muslims entering public office were branded anti-Islamic, and secular courts stripped the clergy of their judicial role.
dff6c83315631a3a:en: The 1973 Oil Boom — How Money Brought Down the Regime
dfb70b228aaddd38:en: • Import bottlenecks — ships waited for months at Khorramshahr port while cargo rotted
6706de5b41d4189c:en: • Inflation of 15–25% from 1975–77, along with a real estate and construction bubble
649d7913d852e083:en: • An explosion in military spending — Iran became the single largest purchaser of US weapons (over $10 billion in orders between 1972–77)
0d66f3ec7686a461:en: • Rural collapse and rising food imports, alongside visibly extreme inequality
654c156ac18e11ea:en: • When oil prices fell, an anti-profiteering crackdown led to the arrest of thousands of merchants, turning even the bazaar, the regime's last non-state social base, against it
14a1a6ea2868b889:en:
1978.01.07

The state-run newspaper Ettela'at published an article branding Khomeini a British agent. Two days later, seminary students were shot dead in the Qom protests.
467e95c77e7d707a:en:
1978.02.18

The Tabriz uprising — began with the 40th-day mourning (Chehelom) for the Qom victims. From then on, the pattern of sacrifice → 40-day mourning → new sacrifice, the Shia mourning cycle, became the engine driving the revolution. It spread to Yazd, Isfahan, Shiraz, Mashhad, and Tehran.
5b9a9c64b7a4da7e:en:
1978.08.19

The Cinema Rex fire in Abadan killed 422 people. At the time it was widely believed to be the work of SAVAK (postrevolutionary trials concluded it was an Islamist arsonist), making it the worst act of terrorism in the world prior to 9/11.
297ea0f1dc5172fd:en:
1978.09.08

Black Friday — on the day martial law was declared, troops opened fire at Jaleh Square in Tehran. Death tolls range from 86–89 according to the government to thousands according to the opposition (an extreme discrepancy). Regardless of the actual number, the possibility of compromise ended on this day.
36bd2b978c789a9b:en:
1978.10.06

Khomeini, expelled from Iraq at the Shah's request, arrives in Neauphle-le-Château near Paris. Paradoxically, gaining access to the international press and a direct phone line to Tehran causes his influence to surge.
7df255c21be4af59:en:
1978.10–12

The general strike of oil workers brings exports to zero by December — a fatal blow to state finances.
0b17c788148490c1:en:
1978.12.10–11

Ashura marches. An estimated 6 to 9 million people (over 10% of the population) nationwide — estimates from the opposition and press.
edb292fbc74984d2:en:
1979.01.16

The Shah departs "on vacation." He never returns, dying in Cairo in 1980.
3c1d339f581e2d6d:en:
1979.02.01

Khomeini returns home. Famously, when asked how he felt about returning, he replied "Hich (nothing)". On February 11, the Supreme Military Council declares neutrality, and the state collapses.
bb21f2e774467b62:en:
1979.03.30

Referendum: a single question — "Islamic Republic — yes or no." 98.2% in favor. Alternatives like a 'Democratic Republic' were not on the ballot.
bfd81d7fa09e801e:en:
1979.12

The constitutional referendum passes. The secular draft had no Velayat-e Faqih, but the clergy-dominated Assembly of Experts inserted it.
8d8edd45b2ea65a0:en: Regarding revolution deaths, the Islamic Republic officially claims 60,000 martyrs, but academic research estimates 2,000 to 3,000 across the entire 1978–79 period. It is one of the largest gaps between official figures and academic estimates in modern history.
1e77f01f7604cb93:en: The 'Guardianship of the Jurist', formalized by Khomeini in his 1970 Najaf lectures, was a break from over 1,000 years of mainstream Shia quietism. The mainstream view held that all governments during the Occultation (Ghaybah) of the 12th Imam lacked legitimacy, and that clerics should guide rather than rule. Even Khomeini himself wrote in a 1943 work, "I do not say that government must be in the hands of the jurist."
4bd91ae9e4804538:en: What matters is that he concealed this agenda throughout the revolution. In Paris, he told Western journalists that clergy would not hold public office and that he himself would return to Qom. And nearly all Grand Ayatollahs rejected Velayat-e Faqih — Khoei of Najaf, Shariatmadari of Qom (who was stripped of his marja status in 1982 and subjected to the unprecedented punishment of house arrest), Golpaygani, and later Montazeri. Sistani of Najaf still maintains quietism today. In other words, Iran's system is an exception that mainstream Shia Islam has never endorsed.
c3bccc9a1a373fc0:en: Takeover of the Revolution and the Hostage Crisis
7b0e558a485d3fbb:en: • Elimination of the liberals: The provisional Bazargan government had no control over the Revolutionary Committees, the Revolutionary Courts (led by the 'Hanging Judge' Khalkhali, who executed hundreds in 1979 alone), or the newly created IRGC (founded May 5, 1979), and it resigned two days after the embassy takeover.
f5b68b5ce1ca20c8:en: • Elimination of the left: The Cultural Revolution of April 1980 shut down universities for about three years and purged tens of thousands of professors and students.
62d6ca9fa5c9ce27:en: • Elimination of the nationalists: The first president, Bani-Sadr (who won 75.6% of the vote in 1980), was impeached in June 1981 and fled into exile in Paris.
f63e2742d3fb6c5f:en: • Terror and counter-terror of 1981–82: A bomb by the MEK at IRP headquarters killed Chief Justice Beheshti and about 70 others, and in August, the president and prime minister were killed simultaneously in a bombing. The state's retaliation was overwhelming — Amnesty International recorded 2,946 executions in 1981 alone. Ali Khamenei became president after his right arm was permanently paralyzed in an assassination attempt in 1981.
08e0513a270f6c44:en: • 1988 prison massacre: Immediately after the MEK's invasion operation, a fatwa from Khomeini led to the mass execution of prisoners. Tehran's 'Death Committee' included Ebrahim Raisi, who would later become president (the basis for his nickname "the Butcher of Tehran"). Death toll estimates: Montazeri's memoir says 2,800 to 3,800; HRW and Amnesty say 2,800 to 5,000; the MEK claims 30,000 (unverified). Montazeri, who criticized this, was removed from his position as successor in March 1989, creating a succession vacuum when Khomeini died three months later.
ff1994f8cf73f227:en: The hostage crisis began on November 4, 1979, and ended after 444 days with 52 hostages, minutes after Reagan's inauguration on January 20, 1981. The trigger was the U.S. allowing the Shah to enter the country for cancer treatment, which Iranians read as a prelude to "another 1953." Khomeini retroactively endorsed it, calling it "the Second Revolution, greater than the First," and indeed used it as leverage to purge the liberals and pass the December constitution. In April 1980, the U.S. severed diplomatic relations — with Switzerland representing U.S. interests and Pakistan representing Iranian interests, a structure that has remained unchanged for 46 years.
dcd45ffca912b890:en: The Machine Called the Islamic Republic — How It Works, and Why It Stopped
eb6521a5e82b6281:en: Iran has a dual structure of elected and unelected bodies. For every elected body, an unelected body screens candidates before the vote, and another unelected body can overturn the results after the vote. Understanding this structure resolves the question, "Iran has elections, so why does nothing change?"
d30c9102ac019891:en: • Determining the general policies of the system and supervising their implementation
38f8752e1996c039:en: • Appointment authority — 6 clerics of the Guardian Council, head of the Judiciary, head of the state broadcaster (IRIB), IRGC Commander-in-Chief, Chief of the regular army, Chief of the Joint Staff, commanders of each branch of the armed forces
1108b0514ec649d1:en: • Mediating disputes among the three branches of government, resolving deadlocks through the Expediency Council
aa547902e3643973:en: • Confirmation of the President's election (Tanfiz) — the President only takes office once the Supreme Leader signs off
a27db975c2aa4cde:en: • Authority to dismiss the President (after a Supreme Court ruling or a parliamentary vote of no confidence)
a16f18f6744a16ec:en: The real power beyond the constitution is even greater — appointing Friday prayer leaders in cities across the country (a nationwide political network), control of the Bonyads, and representatives of the Supreme Leader stationed in every ministry, university, IRGC unit, and provincial government. It is estimated that there are about 2,000 directly appointed positions across the state and quasi-state sectors.
43620a953d349c8b:en:
Assembly of Experts
Assembly of Experts88 clerics, 8-year term, directly electedElects and dismisses the Supreme Leader. However, all candidates are vetted by the Guardian Council, half of whose members are appointed by the Supreme Leader — a closed loop in which the leader picks the body that picks the leader. It has never exercised substantive oversight. In the March 2024 election, Rohani, with 24 years of experience, was disqualified
85f9e430b73c4c19:en:
Guardian Council
Guardian Council6 clerics (appointed by the Leader) + 6 jurists (nominated by the head of the Judiciary, confirmed by Parliament)① Reviews all legislation for compliance with Islam and the constitution (having rejected the anti-torture law, accession to CEDAW, the FATF convention, the press freedom law, etc.) ② Oversight of elections. In 1991 it interpreted its own oversight as "approbative supervision" (nezarat-e estesvabi), thereby gaining the power to reject candidates without stating reasons and to nullify results. This is the single most consequential manipulation in Iran's constitutional order since 1989
8ac2ff2cee8699c8:en:
Expediency Council
Expediency CouncilAround 40 members, all appointed by the LeaderMediates deadlocks between Parliament and the Guardian Council on the basis of "the interest of the system" (maslahat). Established in 1988 by Khomeini's order
ed02ae9ef9294be9:en: Supreme National Security Council (SNSC)Chaired by the President, with the heads of the three branches, the Chief of the Joint Staff, two representatives of the Supreme Leader, the Ministers of Foreign Affairs/Interior/Intelligence, and the commanders of the IRGC and the regular armyThe actual venue where decisions on nuclear issues, war, and peace are made. However, every decision requires the Supreme Leader's approval. This, not the Cabinet, is the real government
c1b348ff69b1d623:en: Parliament (Majlis)290 seats, 4-year term, 5 seats reserved for religious minoritiesApproves the budget, impeachment, and ratification of treaties. However, every bill can be vetoed and every candidate is pre-screened
462563925c78e868:en: President4-year term, one re-election allowedHead of the executive branch, but has no authority over the military, judiciary, broadcasting, or the IRGC economy. The post of Prime Minister was abolished in the 1989 constitutional amendment
b0948750024775e0:en: Every President in history has been broken by the system
972a8c4d324def77:en: Banisadr was impeached and exiled (1981), all of Khatami's reform legislation was rejected, even the hardliner Ahmadinejad clashed with the Supreme Leader in 2011 and had his close aides purged, and Rohani even had his candidacy for the Assembly of Experts disqualified in 2024 after the nuclear deal collapsed. The presidency is the place where the people's mandate is neutralized.
2654388cc326a5ca:en: The IRGC's Economic Empire and the Bonyads
f5ba7fe0dbd4eb39:en: • Khatam al-Anbiya Construction Headquarters (GHORB) — the IRGC's engineering conglomerate that originated in postwar reconstruction projects around 1990. Over 812 registered companies, about 25,000 employees. Phases 13, 14, 15/16, and 22–24 of the South Pars gas field, Line 7 of the Tehran Metro, dams, pipelines, and ports. In 2009, through a rigged privatization, it acquired a 51% stake in the Telecommunication Company of Iran (TCI) for about $7.8 billion, seizing control of the national telecommunications network.
d3daa0060c01c739:en: • Bonyads (Foundations) — quasi-state foundations built on property confiscated during the Pahlavi era, accountable only to the Supreme Leader, tax-exempt, and free from public audit. These include the Mostazafan Foundation (Foundation of the Oppressed), Astan Quds Razavi at the shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad, the Martyrs and Veterans Foundation, and the Imam Khomeini Relief Committee. Reuters estimated in 2013 that the assets of Setad (EIKO) were worth about $95 billion.
5eed5a0881062aba:en: • Caution — the most abused statistic: claims about the IRGC's share of the Iranian economy range from one-third to as much as 80%, with the higher figures mostly coming from opposition-aligned sources. No verifiable figure exists. The most defensible statement is that "IRGC-affiliated entities are the largest operators in energy, construction, and telecommunications, and have received a large volume of no-bid contracts."

3596779bb6a20035:en: This system is designed to operate through participation. Absorbing discontent through elections is the core function of this machine, yet it has lost half of its participating voters in just 10 years. Boycotts have become the dominant strategy of the opposition, and the government's own statistics — which it has an incentive to inflate — are recording that collapse.
ccf0bf1a3945dcbc:en: The most important precedent in this document
ec2dc023dc659657:en: When Khomeini died in June 1989, Ali Khamenei was not a marja (source of emulation) but a Hojatoleslam, one rank lower. At the time, the constitution required marja status for the Supreme Leader. Nevertheless, coordinated by Rafsanjani, the Assembly of Experts elected him as an 'interim' leader (60 out of 74 votes), and then on July 28 of that same year, a constitutional referendum removed the marja requirement itself, which was reconfirmed in August. In 1994, the faculty of the Qom seminary 'declared' him a marja, but many grand ayatollahs, including Montazeri and Sistani, never recognized him as such.
8a7c54544f7a018c:en: The principle established here: the Supreme Leader's qualifications are not a binding constraint, but an obstacle that the ruling coalition can remove in order to install the candidate it wants. The fact that in March 2026 Mojtaba Khamenei could be elected through an online vote with even lower religious credentials than his father is because the requirement had already been removed back in 1989. A maneuver from 37 years ago made today's hereditary succession possible.
54631b21699d19a0:en: • Principlists (conservatives) — Support the Supreme Leader, economically statist and populist, hardline toward the West. Includes the traditional right (the Combatant Clergy Association) and the security/technocratic right (Ghalibaf, Speaker of Parliament, former IRGC Air Force commander and mayor of Tehran).
a748c8703c75a2cd:en: • Paydari Front — The ultra-hardline extreme pole. Founded in 2011 by followers of Mesbah Yazdi, its ideology is an unconstrained clerical absolutism holding that popular legitimacy is meaningless, combined with Mahdism (apocalypticism). Its seats surged from 8 in 2020 to 79 (27%) in 2024, and Mojtaba Khamenei has been reported to be this faction's patron — meaning the Supreme Leader himself now comes from that faction.
ed0d1d34a553b1d7:en: • Reformists — The Khatami lineage. Severely weakened, and trapped in a dilemma: if they participate they are used by the system, and if they boycott they fade away.
b527e552f555108b:en: • Technocrats/centrists — The Rafsanjani–Rouhani–Zarif–Larijani space. Repeatedly purged for arguing that lifting sanctions and normalizing the market were conditions for the regime's survival.
853e3c3ab9af0d17:en: • And the real axis — Through the 2020s, and especially through the 2025–26 war, the real dividing line has become not clerical factions but clerics versus securocrats. Iran is transitioning into a military-security state wearing a clerical mask, and the command reshuffle of August 2026 accelerated that pace.
a9ed6937ee0a4ead:en: Five Doctrines Forged by the Eight-Year War
b6558060f4c11e35:en: Every means Iran used in 2026 — missiles, proxies, self-sufficient production, martyrdom mobilization, distrust of international institutions — was all forged in this war. This chapter carries the heaviest weight in Part Ⅰ.
9721f01d392c6f11:en: The immediate point of contention was the Shatt al-Arab waterway. The 1975 Algiers Agreement had moved the border to the centerline of the waterway, but Saddam Hussein publicly tore up the agreement on September 17, 1980, and invaded five days later. Behind this lay fear of Khomeini's appeal to Iraq's Shia majority to export the revolution, and Saddam's ambition to become the leader of the Arab world in place of Egypt, which had been isolated after Camp David.
2d6bb71fb8ee0ae7:en: 1980.9–10Battle of KhorramshahrIraqi occupation. Iran calls this city the 'City of Blood (Khuninshahr)'. About 7,000 killed on each side
8dbea79a7dba75e4:en: 1982.4–5Operation Beit ol-MoqaddasRecapture of Khorramshahr. 19,000 Iraqi prisoners. At this point Saddam proposed a ceasefire, but Khomeini rejected it and advanced into Iraqi territory — the turning point that prolonged the war by 6 more years
b5cf0a1d692a6f42:en: 1986.2–3Operation Dawn 8 / Faw PeninsulaIran's greatest victory. Landed and occupied Iraq's only Gulf coast
709fff14ed802c4f:en: 1987.1–4Operation Karbala-5 (Battle of Basra)The largest battle of the war and Iran's last major offensive. Iranian casualties of 40,000–65,000. Volunteer recruitment collapsed afterward
a49ec6c4c317664f:en: 1988.4Iraq's recapture of FawRecovered in about 35 hours through massive use of chemical weapons. The Iranian front then collapsed
8df5f5f272fb2a5b:en: Urban Warfare — Where Missile Doctrine Was Born
279918b89033d2c1:en: In the 'War of the Cities' waged over five rounds from 1984–88, Iraq directly struck Iranian cities with Scud and improved Al-Hussein missiles. In the final campaign of January–February 1988, Iraq launched 533 ballistic missiles, hitting 414 of them, and 2,312 civilians were killed. Tehran alone was hit by 118 missiles over 52 days, and about 1 million people fled the city every night.
ac25d3448f58c7af:en: Iran had no means of retaliation whatsoever. This sense of helplessness is the founding experience behind what is today the largest ballistic missile force in the Middle East. The missiles that flew into Israeli cities in 2024 and 2026 are the doctrinal descendants of the Al-Hussein missiles that fell on Tehran in 1988.
73437f0b2ef8f647:en: Chemical Weapons and the Silence of the International Community
23cb6708dcd0f2b8:en: • From October 1983, Iraq systematically used mustard gas, tabun, and sarin, expending more than 100,000 chemical shells. More than 100,000 Iranians were victims of chemical weapons, and even decades later more than 70,000 are still receiving treatment.
307e4af307e00d02:en: • In June 1987, mustard gas was dropped on Sardasht, a city of 12,000 people, killing 130 and wounding 8,000. Iran calls this the first use of chemical weapons on a city since Hiroshima. In March 1988 at Halabja, 3,200–5,000 Kurdish civilians were killed.
13a184d40f91c91f:en: • What is decisive is the international community's response. UN Security Council statements in 1984–85 did not name Iraq, and Resolution 582 in 1986 condemned the use [of chemical weapons] without identifying the perpetrator. Not a single resolution between 1986 and 1988 named Iraq. Furthermore, declassified documents show that the United States continued providing targeting intelligence to Iraq even while knowing it was using chemical weapons.
b8ea6f45f79efd5d:en: In the Tanker War, which began in 1981 and intensified in 1984, according to Lloyd's tallies 546 merchant ships were damaged and about 430 civilian sailors were killed (283 attacks by Iraq, 168 by Iran). The United States intervened with Operation Earnest Will (July 1987–September 1988, the largest convoy operation since World War II), reflagging Kuwaiti tankers under the American flag and escorting them, and with Operation Praying Mantis (April 18, 1988, the largest surface engagement by the US Navy since World War II), which struck the Iranian navy.
db9931dffe18e644:en: Then on July 3, 1988, the cruiser USS Vincennes shot down Iran Air Flight 655, a scheduled flight from Bandar Abbas to Dubai, killing all 290 people aboard (including 66 children). The United States did not issue a formal apology and settled in 1996 for $131.8 million. The captain received a commendation medal that made no mention of the shootdown. Tehran interpreted this as "a signal that the US was entering the war", and two weeks later Khomeini accepted the ceasefire resolution.
be9ed0bde938a90c:en: Upon accepting UN Resolution 598 on July 17, 1988, Khomeini's words are still quoted today — "Making this decision is more deadly than drinking poison. (…) Happy are those who departed through martyrdom. Unhappy am I that I have remained alive." The 8-year war ended with no change in territory and no reparations, reverting to the terms of the 1975 Algiers Accord.
16a8b0e2bfc4f56d:en: Total Losses, and the Five Doctrines That Remained
e407ffa9997db58a:en: Total deaths are estimated at about 500,000 (Iran's official war dead numbering 123,220–160,000, with 320,000–500,000 wounded), and the economic cost was about $627 billion for Iran and about $561 billion for Iraq. The Gulf states lent Iraq $37–60 billion — another reason Iran does not trust the Arab Gulf states.
23272dd937b19da3:en: • Missiles as a substitute for air power. The experience of having no means to counter the Al-Hussein → the region's largest missile force
41914b1e57e5592e:en: • Self-sufficient production (Khodkafa'i). The experience of fighting under a total arms embargo → domestic arms production, and later domestic enrichment
4e0c910870f41f24:en: • Martyrdom and forward defense. The institutionalization of the Basij mobilization culture, and the logic of "fighting on someone else's land" → the proxy network
546633f5e7d93240:en: • Structural distrust of international institutions. The fact that the Security Council did not even name the country that used chemical weapons is the basis of Iran's standard response today to demands from the IAEA and Security Council — "International law has never protected us." This sentiment also underlies Iran's legal denial of the 2025 snapback sanctions
7b95abfc3713098e:en: • Deterrence must be built by oneself. The experience that no outside guarantor ever intervened → enrichment as insurance, not as an energy source
5ca8dc9c717df387:en: Israel–Iran — A Nation That Went From Ally to Enemy
ebd61da3b4e7e266:en: Hard to imagine now, but Iran was once Israel's largest crude oil supplier and an intelligence ally. Understanding how this relationship flipped shows that the hostility of 2026 is not religious destiny but a product shaped by the Cold War and the regional order.
9f6f39a360d1caa8:en: • In 1948, Iran, following Turkey, became the second Muslim-majority country to de facto recognize Israel.
5b1414d74bc19837:en: • Ben-Gurion's 'alliance of the periphery' doctrine — a strategy of joining hands with non-Arab states surrounding the Arab world. The 1958 Trident Agreement institutionalized trilateral intelligence cooperation between Mossad, Turkey's MİT, and Iran's SAVAK, targeting Ba'athist Iraq and Syria. Mossad and SAVAK even jointly supported Iraq's Kurdish rebels (Barzani).
40b30147558e04ed:en: • Oil: After the Suez was closed by the 1967 war, Iran became Israel's major crude oil supplier, with the jointly owned Eilat–Ashkelon Pipeline serving as the conduit.
bc844e5a5e5874a1:en: • From 1977 to 1979, a joint surface-to-surface missile development program was even carried out under the name 'Flower Project'.
b4ca120f696c38b7:en: The Break, Yet the Duality of the 1980s
abf4d26e46a3358c:en: In 1979, Khomeini defined Israel as the 'Little Satan' and handed over the building of the Israeli embassy in Tehran to the PLO. However, actual actions differed from the rhetoric. Israel sold weapons to Iran throughout the Iran-Iraq War — about $75 million worth in 1981's 'Operation Seashell', a total of about $500 million from 1981 to 1983, and around 100 Israeli technical advisors stationed in Iran.
c7c3fa8d8e48d24a:en: The culmination was the Iran-Contra affair (1985–86). Using Israel as a conduit, the U.S. handed over TOW anti-tank missiles and Hawk air defense missiles to Iran, and used the proceeds to support the Nicaraguan Contra rebels. In May 1986, former National Security Advisor McFarlane secretly traveled to Tehran but failed, and in November of that year, a Lebanese magazine exposed the affair, shaking American politics. Israel's logic remained the periphery doctrine — the near enemy was Iraq, and Iran was leverage.
d17fb42c6e586e5b:en: Why It Flipped in the 1990s — Four Factors
d21c8889e103e096:en: • Iraq's defeat in 1991 eliminated the common enemy the two countries had shared.
1593b34b3ccacd43:en: • With the collapse of the Soviet Union, Cold War logic disappeared, leaving Iran as the sole remaining revisionist power in the region.
085bb98319e73843:en: • The 1993 Oslo Accords — Israel needed a new threat narrative to keep U.S. strategic attention, and Iran, positioning itself as the leader of the anti-Oslo rejectionist camp, began supporting Hamas and Islamic Jihad.
b9952a833daa45c5:en: • The growth of Hezbollah and Iran's nuclear program turned the threat from rhetoric into reality.
9708f2e4cd1e75b5:en: 2009–10Stuxnet — A joint U.S.-Israeli operation (Olympic Games). Destroyed about 1,000 IR-1 centrifuges at Natanz by manipulating rotation speedsThe first case of a state-on-state cyber-physical attack
bc9c8f584d4bca9f:en: 2010–2012A series of nuclear scientist assassinations — Ali Mohammadi (Jan 2010), Shahriari (Nov 2010), Rezaeinejad (Jul 2011), Ahmadi Roshan (Jan 2012)Presumed to be the work of Mossad
db40db39c91cfd2a:en: 2012.09.27Netanyahu's 'bomb diagram' at the UN General Assembly — drawing a red line on a cartoon bomb, arguing enrichment must be stopped at that stageThe event that imprinted the Iranian nuclear issue as a popular image
92a120a8c3f8cc2b:en: 2013.01–Launch of the 'War Between Wars' in Syria. About 2,000 strikes in 2018 alone, 1,140 deaths since April 2018A long war of attrition to block Iran's entrenchment in Syria
296d469681b9cfdc:en: 2018.01.31Mossad's seizure of Tehran's nuclear archive — removed 50,000 pages of documents and 183 CDs in about six and a half hours. Netanyahu revealed it on April 30, and eight days later Trump withdrew from the nuclear dealThe political staging for the withdrawal
1a5b13ba31d837d8:en: 2019–2021Maritime shadow war — tanker sabotage off Fujairah (May 2019), attacks in the Gulf of Oman (June 2019), the Iranian vessel Saviz struck by limpet mine (April 2021), the Israeli-operated Mercer Street struck (July 2021)A dress rehearsal for the 2026 merchant vessel attack campaign
0379a00f94594786:en: 2020.11.27Assassination of Mohsen Fakhrizadeh — remote-controlled machine gun. Head of Iran's nuclear program ("Iran's Oppenheimer")Prompted the Iranian parliament to pass a law mandating 20% enrichment
4db353e12ddfc780:en: 2021.04.11Natanz power grid sabotage — assessed to have delayed the program by 9 months to 2 yearsImmediately afterward, Iran began 60% enrichment
53fc0d39d2a29714:en: • April 1, 2024 Israel bombs the annex of the Iranian consulate in Damascus, killing 8 people including IRGC general Mohammad Reza Zahedi.
a1b28ed8ca7ea37c:en: • April 13–14, 2024 'True Promise' — Iran launches the first-ever direct attack on Israeli soil using about 170 drones, roughly 30 cruise missiles, and about 120 ballistic missiles. The US, UK, France, and Jordan jointly intercepted, shooting down about 99%. It was also a moment that revealed the asymmetry of about $1 billion in defense cost versus $80–100 million in attack cost.
06e5e6e6ef28c057:en: • October 1, 2024 About 180 ballistic missiles in retaliation for the deaths of Haniyeh (assassinated in Tehran in July) and Nasrallah. Israel's counterattack on October 26 destroyed Iran's air defense network.
5e0fc8c3b70119b1:en: • June 13–24, 2025, the so-called '12-Day War' (a media/common name, not used in parliamentary briefings of various countries) — Israel's Rising Lion (over 200 fighter jets, over 330 munitions on about 100 targets) eliminated IRGC Commander-in-Chief Salami, Chief of Staff Bagheri, Aerospace Force Commander Hajizadeh, and 9–10 nuclear scientists within hours of the war's start. On June 22, the US joined with Midnight Hammer, dropping 14 GBU-57 bunker-buster bombs from 7 B-2s on Fordow and Natanz, while submarines fired about 20 Tomahawks at Isfahan. Iran counterattacked with over 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones and struck the Al Udeid base in Qatar before a ceasefire on June 24. Casualties: Iran 1,060–1,190, Israel 32–33.
0e0444593f1a84a1:en: There are two reasons the 12-Day War is decisive for understanding the 2026 war. First, it set a precedent that the world does not collapse even when the US directly strikes Iran's mainland nuclear facilities. Second, two-thirds of Iran's missile launchers and most of its air defense network were already destroyed at this time. Iran in February 2026 was far more exposed than it had been 8 months earlier.
f09ec22e033def24:en: The Axis of Resistance — 40 Years to Build, 14 Months to Collapse
d085662bd2750755:en: Iran's deterrence strategy was to create buffer zones outside its borders. How this network was built and why it collapsed in 2024 is a precondition for the 2026 invasion decision.
8793e288c22cd742:en: • In 1982, right after Israel's invasion of Lebanon, Iran dispatched about 1,500 IRGC instructors to the Bekaa Valley to establish it.
ba91e7b63a76c1a0:en: • 1983: the April Beirut US Embassy bombing (63 dead, most of the CIA's Beirut station killed) and the October Marine barracks bombing (241 US troops and 58 French troops killed). Reagan ordered a withdrawal 4 months later — this is where the lesson was created that asymmetric attacks can make a superpower retreat.
6500523450ca9ec1:en: • Israel's withdrawal from South Lebanon in 2000 became Hezbollah's founding myth, and in the 34-day war of 2006 it survived while firing about 4,000 rockets.
5c8d60c11a81934d:en: • Its intervention in the Syrian civil war in 2013 (the Battle of Qusayr) transformed it from a 'resistance organization' into a regional expeditionary force, while simultaneously losing support in the Sunni Arab world.
ae0271743ec14ebc:en: • Its arsenal grew from about 14,000 rockets in 2006 to over 150,000 in 2023, and Iran's support was estimated at about $700 million per year (2018 US Treasury Department estimate).
38c0d59e1e233f15:en: • And then collapse in 2024: on September 17–18, simultaneous explosions of pagers and walkie-talkies killed 42 and wounded 3,500–4,000 (about 1,500 combatants lost combat capability), Nasrallah's death on September 27 (after a 32-year tenure), a ground invasion in October, and a ceasefire on November 27. Iran's greatest asset, built over 40 years, was neutralized in just two months.
177436f992a33b70:en: Iraq — The Country the US Handed Over to Iran
e8b8da075682ae86:en: The US invasion of Iraq in 2003 was the single greatest transfer of power to Iran in modern history. This is because the Sunni Ba'athist state that had contained Iran disappeared, and Shia parties that had been exiled in Iran in the 1980s came to power. SCIRI was founded in Tehran in 1982, and its militia, the Badr Corps, fought on Iran's side in the Iran-Iraq War. The Dawa Party took refuge in Iran in the 1980s and produced two prime ministers, Maliki and Abadi.
edaf8372fae8fc14:en: Syria — The Oldest Ally, The Greatest Loss
585313ccbe558588:en: In February 1979, Syria was the first Arab country to recognize the Islamic Republic and the only Arab nation to side with Iran in the Iran-Iraq War. In return, Iran supplied free or discounted crude oil throughout the 1980s. This alliance was the backbone of the Tehran–Baghdad–Damascus–Beirut land corridor.
a1f0fac390e04432:en: In the 2011 civil war, Iran mobilized over 80,000 pro-Assad Shia fighters, deploying the IRGC and Hezbollah as well as the Afghan Fatemiyoun and Pakistani Zainebiyoun brigades, with spending estimated at $30–50 billion (a contested figure). And then, on December 8, 2024, Damascus fell. Assad fled into exile in Moscow, and the Iranian embassy was looted.
83525e944841ab42:en: The collapse of the Assad regime is the real turning point of this war. With the land supply route cut off, Hezbollah could not rearm in 2025–26, and Iran permanently lost its deterrence against northern Israel. Half of the calculation behind the U.S. and Israel judging in February 2026 that they could strike the Iranian mainland comes from this.
74901ac3f1872c89:en: The Houthis — the only axis that grew stronger
c9e14d404baab548:en: Starting from an ideological bond in the 1990s (the Houthi brothers studied in Qom), support became overt after the capture of Sanaa in 2014. The intervention of a Saudi-led coalition of 9 countries in March 2015 caused a humanitarian catastrophe with over 377,000 deaths in total from 2014 to 2021 (about 60% from indirect causes such as famine and disease, per UNDP), but it failed to bring down the Houthis.
38b54f8949dacd36:en: The Red Sea campaign from November 2023 involved more than 100 attacks, the sinking of 4 ships, more than 15 crew deaths, and inflicted around $200 billion in costs on the global economy in 2024. The Houthis, who entered the war in March 2026, were the only member of the Axis of Resistance that remained intact — indeed, even strengthened.
2af576605318ff67:en: The Saudi–Iran rivalry and the Gulf's calculations
f8cb904220714364:en:
1979

The revolution directly attacked the religious legitimacy of the Saudi monarchy. Following the Grand Mosque seizure in Mecca in November of the same year (about 270 deaths), Saudi Arabia strengthened the powers of the religious police and the ulama, becoming more conservative for decades.
eb1ae5c00e30b147:en:
1987.07

A protest by Iranian pilgrims in Mecca escalated into a clash, resulting in about 400 deaths. In 1988, Saudi Arabia severed diplomatic ties.
b1f87d592c4a3e6d:en:
2016.01

Saudi Arabia executed Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr → the Saudi embassy in Tehran was set on fire → diplomatic relations severed. Bahrain and Sudan also severed ties.
eac3e7ab2c3d5f1f:en:
2020.09

The Abraham Accords — the UAE and Bahrain established diplomatic relations with Israel (later joined by Morocco and Sudan). This was read as the political completion of the encirclement of Iran.
0bb3a281f3b490ad:en:
2023.03.10

China-mediated normalization of Saudi–Iran relations. Ambassadors were exchanged within 2 months, restoring the 1998 cooperation agreement and the 2001 security agreement. However, it did not address the nuclear issue, relations with Israel, or a solution for Yemen at all — in essence it was risk management after Abqaiq.
181ace54bd5783f6:en:
2023.10.07

Hamas's surprise attack halted the Saudi–Israel normalization talks. Riyadh has since made a path to Palestinian statehood a condition.
84bac911578cb191:en:
2026

The war effectively dissolved the Beijing détente. All 6 Gulf states came under attack yet maintained official neutrality, but Saudi Arabia allowed U.S. forces to operate on its own territory, and the UAE completely halted dealings with Iran in August.
6697db7ea3c4db93:en: In this relationship, there were several moments when an agreement was possible, and each was missed. The surprise attack of February 2026 is the last item on that list.
2b15f5339f6a00f7:en: • 1995 — Rafsanjani sent a deliberate opening signal by granting a $1 billion oil field development deal to the American company Conoco, but the Clinton administration nullified it by executive order within days.
1adcfed468582592:en: • 1998 — Khatami's CNN interview on the "Dialogue Among Civilizations." Albright responded, and in 2000 the U.S. acknowledged for the first time its role in the 1953 coup.
9b78a06432fd5cae:en: • 2001 — Substantive cooperation in Afghanistan. At the Bonn conference, Iran persuaded the Northern Alliance, enabling the launch of the Karzai government. Bush's 'Axis of Evil' speech seven weeks later ended this momentum and decisively weakened Iranian reformists.
6f3506416764a167:en: • 2003 — The so-called 'Grand Bargain' fax delivered via the Swiss ambassador. It proposed trading nuclear transparency, resolution of the al-Qaeda issue, cessation of support for Hamas, legitimization of Hezbollah, and acceptance of a two-state solution in exchange for lifting sanctions and providing security guarantees. The Bush administration did not respond and reprimanded the Swiss for delivering it (whether it was approved by the Supreme Leader is still debated today).
67e901278eb6798d:en: • 2013.9.27 — A 15-minute phone call between Rouhani and Obama. The first direct contact at the head-of-state level since 1979.
65d89d2967465b6b:en: • 2015 — The JCPOA was concluded. 2018 — The U.S. withdrew.
977ceaa4f9084fcf:en: • 2021–22 — 8 rounds of talks in Vienna broke down over the IRGC terrorist designation issue and the sequencing of implementation.
5d47a4f2d181a2a1:en: • 2023.9 — A prisoner exchange and the transfer to Qatar of $6 billion held in South Korea (see Ⅰ-11 below).
cb4a124671329739:en: • 2025–26 — The Muscat negotiations, and then a surprise attack right before a deal was reached.
bbc0778735eba24c:en: Nuclear — A Program the U.S. Helped Start
0db4ca3084b668a9:en: Iran's nuclear program began as a gift from the United States. Its starting point was Eisenhower's 1957 'Atoms for Peace' agreement and the Tehran Research Reactor given by the U.S. in 1967.
708f33ac45e93ce7:en: 1957U.S.–Iran civil nuclear agreement (Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace')
c5f4bac7d408ecce:en: 1967The U.S.-supplied Tehran Research Reactor begins operation — initial fuel was 93% highly enriched uranium
cfc59643f9da2db7:en: 1970NPT enters into force. Iran is one of the 62 original signatory states
4c055a72f72a390f:en: 1974The Shah establishes the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) and declares a goal of 23,000MW (23 nuclear power plants) within 20 years. Invests about $1 billion in the French Eurodif enrichment consortium
635e0f1389885a5c:en: 1975Contracts with Germany's Siemens for 2 reactors at Bushehr. The Shah's nuclear weapons intentions during this period remain debated to this day
06fa150004898dd1:en: 1987 · 1994–96Obtains about 500 P-1 centrifuges and P-2 designs from Pakistan's A.Q. Khan network
83c82a6aa0092d94:en: 1991China secretly supplies 1,000kg of UF6 and other materials (undeclared to the IAEA until 2003)
4e09cdb13ae7a572:en: 1995Russia contracts to complete Bushehr — a method of fitting a Russian-type reactor inside a building built by Germany
e7e7bb98145969a3:en: 1999–2003AMAD Plan — a program led by Fakhrizadeh aiming to produce 5 nuclear weapons by 2004
c247695f62052af0:en: 2002.08.14Opposition group NCRI exposes the Natanz enrichment facility and Arak heavy water reactor — the start of the crisis
59c8159d3f6f5c9d:en: • Natanz — the main underground enrichment facility. As of June 2025, about 18,000 centrifuges are underground. The above-ground pilot facility (PFEP) carried out 20%·60% enrichment.
35203a80091676e8:en: • Fordow — secretly built inside a mountain near Qom, exposed in 2009. 80–90m below bedrock, with a scale of about 3,000 units. 20% enrichment in 2021, 60% enrichment from November 2022.
c72981cc4ab449bd:en: • Isfahan UCF — a facility that converts yellowcake into UF6. And crucially, this is also where the tunnel complex believed to hold most of the highly enriched uranium stockpile is located.
b45b30dd32f99b7c:en: • Arak (Khondab) Heavy Water Reactor — a 40MW reactor that, if operated, would have produced about 9kg of plutonium annually (enough for 1–2 nuclear weapons). It has never been loaded with fuel.
c95f9a5a52bbf2da:en: • Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant — Russia supplies the fuel and takes back all spent fuel. In other words, there is no fuel-cycle need that would justify domestic enrichment — the strongest counterargument to Iran's claims.
77507ed681eef9ee:en: • Pickaxe Mountain (Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La) — a new underground complex south of Natanz. 2.7 km², at a depth of 80–100m or more, deeper than Fordow, possibly beyond the reach of conventional bunker-busters. The IAEA has never been allowed inside, and it was struck neither in 2025 nor in 2026.
13ae6d716a380d59:en: • Parchin, Lavizan, Turquzabad, Varamin — sites linked to suspected weaponization or undeclared activities. The Turquzabad and Varamin issues remain unresolved to this day.
6c427fa9b3334652:en: Know just this, and the news becomes readable
1f00e2794cf5e0d3:en: • Why 60% is dangerous. Natural uranium's U-235 is 0.711%, and weapons-grade is 90% or higher. However, the separative work (SWU) is concentrated at the front end — reaching 20% from natural uranium consumes about 90% of the total work, and reaching 60% consumes 98~99%. In other words, a country holding a 60% stockpile is, from an energy standpoint, already nearly weapons-grade, and 60% enrichment has no civilian use whatsoever.
2c0b20f4dd5e3cf2:en: • Centrifuge generations. If the IR-1 produces 0.8~1 SWU per year, the IR-6 produces 6~10 times that. Even keeping the same number of units, simply changing the model collapses the breakout time. In early 2025, the newer models exceeded IR-1 output for the first time.
0dff2351dc0620e5:en: • Breakout time. This is the time required to produce material for one weapon (25kg of U-235 per IAEA standard), and it is an indicator of capability, not intent. Under the JCPOA it was about 12 months → in 2022~23 about 12 days → by late 2024, enough for 5~6 weapons within 2 weeks. As of 2026, calculation itself is impossible — because facilities have been destroyed and, with no inspections, no one knows where the stockpiles are located.
8a61aa538cae8724:en: 2025.06.13440.9 kgEstimate at time of attack (ISIS). The difference between 408 vs 441 is due to differing reference dates and calculation methods, not a contradiction
b0e1b90ac55640bf:en: 2026.08UnknownThe IAEA stated that since June 2025 it "cannot provide any information on the scale, composition, or location of the stockpile"
f43aa1e04672fb8b:en: The 408~441kg 60% stockpile corresponds to 10~11 nuclear weapons' worth upon further enrichment. It is estimated that 60~65% is stored in the Isfahan tunnel, with the rest at Fordow and Natanz (all ISIS estimates).
75b2a41a1c618dbe:en: • AMAD Project (1999~2003) — A program led by Fakhrizadeh to integrate five 10kt-class warheads into Shahab-3 reentry vehicles. It was halted in late 2003, and about 70% of its personnel were transferred to SPND.
0748086001b94b4d:en: • 2007 US NIE — Assessed "with high confidence" that Iran halted its nuclear weapons program in the fall of 2003. This was politically explosive.
ac38370d9340e262:en: • IAEA 2011 Report — Disclosed 12 areas of concern, including detonators, multi-point initiation, hydrodynamic experiments, neutron sources, and reentry vehicle integration.
6d56fd54288fd357:en: • IAEA 2015 Final Assessment — Concluded that before 2003 there was a systematic "coordinated set of activities relevant to the development of a nuclear explosive device", some of which continued until 2009, but that there were no credible indications of weapons activities or diversion of nuclear material after 2009. The Board closed this file, and this was the political precondition for JCPOA implementation.
2898ce504001380b:en: • June 12, 2025 — The IAEA Board acknowledged Iran's non-compliance with safeguards for the first time in about 20 years. Israel attacked the very next day.
73938831276a56ab:en: • November 2025 — The IAEA officially declared that it "lost continuity of knowledge" regarding Iran's nuclear material.
0a05431cd3901e26:en: Iran's official position rests on Khamenei's fatwa prohibiting nuclear weapons (verbally mentioned in 2003, formally cited to the IAEA in 2005) and the "inalienable right" under NPT Article 4. There are two counterarguments — that no certified original document of the fatwa has ever been produced, and that a fatwa is inherently subject to change depending on circumstances. Indeed, in February 2025 there were reports that IRGC commanders demanded the fatwa be rescinded, and in March, Larijani said, "If attacked, Iran will build nuclear weapons."
6f5d90997f28f1ec:en: To state the situation as of August 2026 in one sentence: Iran remains a party to the NPT, but IAEA verification has been effectively suspended since June~July 2025, and completely halted since February 28, 2026. This is the worst kind of gray zone — legally a member state, but practically an unverified state.

62bc5b76c652bfb8:en: This is the core pathology of Iran's economy
9a874e395da9a9de:en: In Iran, at least three and as many as eight exchange rates exist simultaneously. There is the official preferential rate of 42,000 rials (fixed in 2018, used for importing essential goods such as medicine, wheat, and meat), the NIMA rate at which exporting companies are required to sell foreign currency, and the market rate (about 1.9 million rials).
da35ff0435d9095b:en: The gap between 42,000 and 1,900,000 is about 45 times. This difference is rent that goes entirely to those holding import licenses. In other words, sanctions have created suffering for the people while generating enormous wealth for the small number holding licenses. Unifying the exchange rate is recommended by every economist, but it is politically almost impossible because it would immediately cause consumer prices to skyrocket.
bb236fafdb272c38:en: The same logic applies across the entire sanctions-evasion economy. Shadow fleet operators, currency exchange networks, and IRGC-affiliated brokers take the spread. In 2013, Babak Zanjani was arrested on charges of embezzling $2.7 billion in oil payments that should have been remitted. This is the strongest evidence for the claim that "sanctions did not weaken the hardline security forces but instead concentrated power in their hands."
a7b1272899d20db2:en: Subsidies, and the Terror Left Behind by November 2019
ffdf303f779c1f46:en: Despite having the world's 2nd-largest gas reserves and 4th-largest crude oil reserves, Iran suffers from chronic energy shortages. Winter gas shortages of 250 million~300 million㎥ per day, a summer 2024 electricity shortfall of 14,000MW, and in early 2025, 80 out of 600 power plants shut down. The causes are waste created by subsidies, thermal power generation efficiency of just 33%, transmission losses of 13%, gas flaring of 18 billion㎥ annually, and lack of investment. The result was nationwide school and business closures from December 2024 to February 2025, with about 50% of industry shut down. Combined with a water crisis in which 80% of wetlands have dried up, the World Bank now cites water and energy shortages alongside sanctions as factors hindering growth.
f5a70f3233701de8:en: • China — An indispensable partner. It purchases 80~93% of Iran's crude oil, and in March 2021 the two signed a 25-Year Comprehensive Cooperation Agreement. The widely-cited figure of "$400 billion" originated from a trade publication report and has never been confirmed by either government, and actual investment has come nowhere close to that amount.
556fe5dc96a2503f:en: • Russia — A 20-Year Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty in January 2025. However, it contains no mutual defense clause — it only commits to not aiding an aggressor, and in practice Russia did not help Iran in either 2025 or 2026. Trade amounts to only $4~5 billion per year.
395ec500fca6e930:en: • UAE — For 40 years, it served as Iran's window for hard currency, re-export trade, and informal finance. About 30% of Iran's imports (worth $21 billion in 2024) and 90% of Gulf trade passed through it. The UAE's complete shutdown of this route on August 19, 2026 accomplished in a single stroke what 40 years of U.S. sanctions had failed to do.

ef06404d1a7519ac:en: Those Who Have Already Left — Population, Women, Brain Drain, and Ethnic Minorities
172ebaf6154d6245:en: The most frequently overlooked aspect when examining Iranian politics is social indicators. This country's population has already moved in a different direction from the regime.
b4e46abd454165fa:en: • About 33.7 million in 1976 → about 37 million in 1979 → about 92 million in 2025. The population more than doubled during the first 40 years of the Islamic Republic.
33fa21b16736a8c2:en: • The state-encouraged post-revolution baby boom (1979~88) during wartime pushed the annual population growth rate to 3.9~4.0% — one of the highest rates in human history. This generation became the 'youth bulge' that supported Khatami in 1997, drove the protests of 1999 and 2009, and caused the explosion in demand for university education.
702c8a388dfe1aa3:en: • And then followed one of the sharpest fertility collapses in modern history. The total fertility rate fell from 6.5~7.0 in the early 1980s to 2.0 in 2000, and to 1.6~1.7 in 2021 (currently estimated at 1.4~1.5). The state family planning program from 1989~2006 was a globally recognized success story, but in 2012 the Supreme Leader shifted course toward pronatalism, and the 2021 'Youthful Population Law' restricted contraception and abortion — yet the fertility rate did not budge.
ea257efe984756a9:en: • The growth rate is now 0.7~1.2% annually, the median age is 32~33, and by the 2040s the country will become an aged society. There are no funds for pensions. The youth bulge has already passed, which means the pattern of future protests will be different.

The hijab, unequal inheritance and testimony rights, guardianship in marriage and travel, exclusion from the presidency and the highest judicial posts. In a country where women make up 70% of those in medicine and basic sciences, the female employment rate hovers around 15% — this gap is the engine of 'Woman, Life, Freedom'.
e70ff8e7a346010d:en: Iranians abroad are estimated at 4 to 5 million, with more than 30% in the United States. About 60% of Iranian immigrants in the US hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and more than 30% hold a master's or doctorate, making them one of the most highly educated immigrant groups in America. In early 2020, the number of Iranian students enrolled in universities abroad reached about 130,000, an all-time high, and 96% of patents filed by Iranian-born inventors between 2007 and 2012 were filed by those living abroad. In 2024, the Minister of Higher Education admitted that about 25% of university professors had been lost to emigration. The cost estimate often cited is $50 billion a year (World Bank), but this is a rough and contested estimate — for reference, Iran's oil exports in 2019 were under $20 billion.

Nearly half of the 2022 protest deaths came from Kurdistan and Sistan-Baluchestan.
04c2902db468f156:en: • The Baha'i (about 300,000) are not recognized under any provision of the constitution, are barred from university admission and public office, and are subject to property confiscation and imprisonment. By contrast, Jews (about 9,000), the largest Jewish community in the Muslim Middle East, hold one reserved seat in parliament.
8b0d462c1b857e9f:en: Qom and Najaf — The Shia World Never Endorsed the Iranian System
02d60520528fc767:en: Qom was rebuilt in 1922 by Haeri Yazdi, and until 1961 it was home to Borujerdi, the sole supreme marja of the Shia world at the time. His quietism kept Khomeini in check, and only after his death did Khomeini step to the forefront. Today Qom has more than 40,000 seminary students, but since 1980 it has been placed under state oversight through the seminary management council, and its finances also flow through the state and the bonyads — the point where its independence has been compromised.
21f6b610f629712f:en: Najaf is the older and more authoritative center dating from the 11th century, and Sistani (born 1930) is the marja with the largest following in the Shia world. He is a quietist, holding that clergy should advise and safeguard but not rule. Like his call for direct elections in 2004 and his anti-ISIS fatwa in 2014, this is a model in which he intervenes decisively only in existential crises and holds no permanent office.
afcda291da405c27:en: Structural implication: Najaf is the living counter-model to Velayat-e Faqih, and the mainstream of Shia jurisprudence has never accepted Iran's system. The succession question for Sistani, now in his mid-90s, is another massive succession issue for the Shia world.

558440d10dad2d49:en: The Conventional Wisdom That "Full Closure Is Self-Harm" — And the Third Path Iran Found
269396f81fb5dd81:en: Until 2025, the standard expert view was as follows. ① China buys about 90% of Iranian crude, so a blockade would hit that sole customer ② Iran's own exports also depend on Hormuz (the Jask bypass line is essentially non-operational) ③ it would give Gulf Arab states a pretext to enter the conflict ④ precedent of the 5th Fleet and 1988's Praying Mantis ⑤ in Secretary of State Rubio's words, "economic suicide".
baca9700898d6013:en: What Iran did in 2026 was bypass this conventional wisdom. Instead of fully closing the strait, it created a selective passage + toll system (PGSA), letting ships from friendly countries like China, Russia, and India pass while charging others $1–2 million per vessel. It turned the blockade from self-harm into a source of income and a bargaining chip, and this is the technical reason this war has not ended after six months.
9da4c1d987a91439:en: The British Navy's blockade of Abadan in 1951, the Tanker War of 1980–88(even then, over 98% of transiting vessels went unmolested and the strait was never actually closed), the threat over the EU embargo in 2011–12("easier than drinking water"), Rouhani's warnings and tanker attacks in 2018–19, Abqaiq in 2019, and in June 2025, the Iranian parliament's passage of a closure resolution(the final decision rests with the SNSC, so it was not implemented). A card that had only ever been threatened for decades was actually used for the first time in 2026.
b1ba98fa4e0d3b08:en: Since its founding in 1974, the IEA has invoked collective action six times — the 1991 Gulf War, 2005 Katrina, 2011 Libya, 2022 Ukraine(twice), and the largest-ever release of 400 million barrels on March 11, 2026. National strategic reserves (as of end-2025) stand at approximately 1.4 billion barrels for China, 413 million for the US SPR, 263 million for Japan's government reserve, and 79 million for South Korea.

fb3b211464a5c339:en: Korea has become deeply entangled with this region three times — recouping oil money through the construction boom of the 1970s, paying the price of sanctions in the 2010s, and now receiving the bill again in 2026.
826c90708a5a0952:en: The 1970s — Recouping the Oil Shock through Construction Exports
aa5b13c91ff53a66:en: • It began in June 1973 when Samhwan Corporation won the contract for the Khaibar–Al-Ula highway (175km) in Saudi Arabia. A famous story tells of how, to shorten the construction period during the pilgrimage season, thousands of torches were lit in the desert for night work, and when this reached King Faisal, it is said to have led to an additional $65 million contract.
52e184be01910f39:en: • Overseas construction contract amounts exploded from a cumulative $423 million during 1965–73 to $34.66 billion during 1974–81, of which 94% was in the Middle East. During the same period, overseas construction contract value came close to half of total exports, and the number of dispatched workers exceeded 100,000 in 1979 and more than 150,000 annually during 1981–83. In 1981, Korea ranked 2nd in the world in overseas construction contracts.
985750a3e46255e5:en: • Significance: Recouping money accumulated in oil-producing countries through construction exports and thereby offsetting the burden of oil prices and the current account deficit was the key channel through which Korea overcame the first oil shock relatively quickly.
7e7a46de43202e0a:en: Nevertheless, the shock was severe. Due to the first oil shock, the growth rate fell from 14.8% in 1973 to around 7% in 1975, and consumer prices rose 24.7% in 1975. The second shock was even worse, resulting in negative growth in 1980 (−1.6% under the revised national accounts, −5.2% under the old accounts, figures vary by source), wholesale prices +38.9%, and a current account deficit of $5.3 billion, with domestic oil prices raised 7 times, a cumulative 337%, from March 1979 to November 1981.

10a78ef0924424e4:en: The 2020 Cheonghae Unit Precedent — The Root of the Current Debate
1c5addb22e006646:en: On January 21, 2020, the government decided not to join the U.S.-led International Maritime Security Construct (IMSC) but instead to independently expand the operational area of the Cheonghae Unit. The area was expanded 3.5 times from 1,130km in the Gulf of Aden to about 3,960km, including the Strait of Hormuz, while only two liaison officers were sent to the IMSC. The stated justification was "protecting our citizens and vessels," and this was carried out without National Assembly approval.
ae77fe1b7fcecbc5:en: This compromise is the precedent that complicates the 2026 troop dispatch debate. Interpretations clash over whether participation in a multinational force requires National Assembly approval, since it constitutes entry into combat, versus whether it is unnecessary if it is merely an expansion of an existing operation, and the government's April 2026 legal interpretation ("escorting merchant ships does not require approval, but securing a detour route through the Red Sea does") is also based on this framework.

Death of Mahsa Amini and 'Woman, Life, Freedom.' A decisive signal that the regime's social base had thinned. In September of the same year, the Vienna nuclear talks finally collapsed.

China-mediated normalization of Saudi–Iran relations. It seemed like a détente phase was opening.

Hamas's surprise attack ('Al-Aqsa Flood'). About 1,200 dead and 251 taken hostage on the Israeli side. It is the starting point of full-scale regional escalation, and the Saudi–Israel normalization talks also stop here.
8c9d4d8151e5a931:en:
2024.04 · 10

Two rounds of the first-ever direct missile exchanges between Iran and Israel. In the October counterattack, Iran's air defense network was destroyed, opening its airspace.
bd369955986ea4da:en:
2024.09–11

Pager explosions, elimination of Nasrallah, ground invasion, ceasefire in November. Hezbollah, built up over 40 years, was neutralized in just two months.
72c4b0aa13910624:en:
2024.12.08

Collapse of the Assad regime. Iran's overland supply route is cut, and the 'axis of resistance' is effectively dismantled.
f3189204c0b23754:en:
2025.06.13–24

The 12-Day War. Israel's Rising Lion + America's Midnight Hammer. A precedent is set that the world does not collapse even when the United States directly strikes Iran's homeland nuclear facilities. Two-thirds of the launchers and most of the air defense network are lost at this time.
f6d182fb0bbc7452:en:
2025.09.28

Restoration of UN snapback sanctions. The 30-day deadline triggered by the E3 on August 28 expires, leading to automatic restoration (the Russia–China extension resolution of September 26–27 is rejected). Since the E3's own triggering authority itself was set to expire on October 18, this was using the last chance. On October 18, Iran declares the end of the JCPOA.
a5fb7a73a1dd35e4:en:
2025.12.28–

Iran's largest anti-government protests, beginning with the shutdown of the Grand Bazaar in Tehran. The trigger was the rial's collapse and 42% inflation, and it is estimated to have spread to more than 200 cities across 31 provinces, with about 5 million people nationwide participating on January 8–9. A total internet blackout and live-fire crackdowns followed.
2cb41bae2487c17e:en:
2026.01

The EU designates the IRGC as a terrorist organization. The United States deploys 2 carrier strike groups and hundreds of aircraft to the Middle East — the largest deployment since the 2003 invasion of Iraq.
529b650c89cf041b:en: Protest death toll — a figure that must always be cited alongside caveats
3d6246de13ac3c2e:en: The death toll from the 2025~26 protests is the figure with the widest discrepancy in this document. The Iranian government says 3,117, the Iran Human Rights organization says 3,428, HRANA's confirmed count is 7,015 (as of February 5), some Western reports cite 30,000 to 36,500 for just the two days of January 8–9 alone, and the international estimated range is 12,000~43,000. Because of the total internet blackout from January 8 onward, independent verification is effectively impossible, so the higher figures are safest treated as unverified estimates.
0121260518a95cc4:en: Why February 2026 — six conditions came together all at once
d7107527179b7f24:en: • Loss of deterrence — With Hezbollah's destruction (Sep–Nov 2024), Assad's collapse (Dec 2024), and Hamas's exhaustion, Iran lost the proxy fronts through which it could retaliate. 40 years of investment collapsed in 14 months.
930ac7d1f09f728f:en: • Collapse of air defense network — Through two rounds of strikes in October 2024 and June 2025, key assets such as the S-300 and two-thirds of missile launchers were already gone.
39e4b24dc9d2b42d:en: • Precedent secured — In June 2025, the United States directly struck Iran's homeland nuclear facilities, and it did not lead to escalation. The political threshold had already been lowered.
484232e9840480d8:en: • Diplomatic channels closed — With the restoration of snapback sanctions in September 2025, the incentive of sanctions relief was exhausted, and in October Iran declared the end of the JCPOA. It was a state where neither side had anything left to gain from negotiation.
3ecb339b39409d8d:en: • Regime vulnerability — At the end of 2025, protests involving 5 million people and bloody crackdowns, 88% inflation, and the collapse of the rial. The calculation that "it could collapse now" took hold in Washington and Jerusalem.
9b12361437fe42c5:en: • 그리고 검증의 공백 — 2025년 7월 이후 IAEA가 사실상 들어가지 못하면서, "이란이 무엇을 하고 있는지 아무도 모른다"는 상태가 공격의 명분과 공포를 동시에 키웠습니다.
08cf69db62478658:en: Part Ⅰ의 결론 — 여섯 개의 관통선
c35296341688e28c:en: • 석유와 주권이 1901년부터 지금까지의 관통선입니다. 다르시 이권 → 국유화 → 1953년 쿠데타 → 지대국가 → 제재 → 호르무즈. 이란의 모든 정치 위기에는 석유 조항이 있습니다.
23330ec135493d58:en: • 외세 개입이 체제의 정통성 서사입니다. 1907·1941·1953·1980(사담)·2018·2025~26. 이것이 정권을 정당화하지는 않지만, 정권을 혐오하는 민족주의 이란인조차 외침에는 저항하는 이유를 설명하며, 외부 압박이 왜 한 번도 그 지지자들이 예측한 정치 변화를 만들어내지 못했는지도 설명합니다.
3995a244b8025f2e:en: • 이 체제의 천재성이자 함정: 공화정의 형식(선거·의회·대통령)에 성직자 거부권을 접붙여 반대를 흡수해 무력화하는 기계를 만들었습니다. 25년간 작동했습니다. 투표율이 80%에서 40%로 무너진 것은 그 기계가 고장났다는 뜻입니다 — 참여를 전제로 설계된 장치이기 때문입니다.
e3cdd2c8bdea8722:en: • 최고지도자의 자격은 법이 아니라 정치입니다. 1989년에 하메네이를 앉히려고 마르자 요건을 삭제했고, 2026년에는 그 삭제를 이용해 그의 아들을 온라인 표결로, 폭격 아래서, IRGC의 압력 속에, 고인의 유언에 반해 앉혔습니다.
95d5231d653bee25:en: • 성직자가 안보 실세에 밀려났습니다. IRGC의 경제 제국, 1999년 하타미에게 보낸 협박 서한, 2009년의 역할, 2026년 전문가회의에 대한 압력, 그리고 지금 페제시키안 위에 선 바히디·레자이 — 모두 한 방향을 가리킵니다. 이슬람공화국은 성직자 외피를 쓴 군사·안보 국가가 되어가고 있습니다.
86ae39660f00b2fc:en: • 사회는 이미 떠났습니다. 출산율 1.6, 법적으로 묶인 고학력 여성, 해외로 나간 학위자, '여성 생명 자유', 공공연한 히잡 불복종, 40%의 투표율. 국가의 자기 서사를 더 이상 받아들이지 않는 인구가, 그것을 대체할 조직을 갖지 못한 상태 — 그것이 2026년 이란의 실제 조건입니다.
58d0d64cd0f906f4:en: 이 전쟁에서 가장 논쟁적인 것은 전쟁의 방식이 아니라 시점입니다. 공격은 협상이 깨져서가 아니라, 협상이 거의 타결되던 순간에 시작됐습니다.
52c8cec946b0ca31:en:
1월

미국이 중동에 병력을 대규모 전개. 항모전단 2개(USS Abraham Lincoln 1월 26일 도착, USS Gerald R. Ford 2월 13일 출항)와 수백 대의 항공기. 규모는 2003년 이라크 침공 이래 최대.
002e807f006a8f60:en:
1월 말

EU가 혁명수비대(IRGC)를 테러조직으로 지정. 미국은 라리자니 등 보안 당국자 5명 제재.
06f5d6c6e73ddaa5:en:
2.02

페제시키안 대통령이 미국과의 핵협상 재개를 지시.
3fee0b182213f43e:en:
2.06

오만 무스카트 간접 협상 개시. 미국 측 스티브 위트코프 특사·재러드 쿠슈너, 그리고 이례적으로 브래드 쿠퍼 중부사령관이 동석 — 협상과 무력 위협을 동시에 얹는 신호. 이란 측 아락치 외교장관. 중재는 오만 외교장관 바드르 알부사이디.
f76292fd4a09aa98:en:
2.11

네타냐후 총리가 트럼프 대통령과 회동해 군사행동을 압박.
9ac5ea9da62149d7:en:
2.17 · 2.20

하메네이가 트럼프의 조건을 공개 거부 → 트럼프가 10일 최후통첩.
bb2de56252202ad9:en:
2.24–27

F-22 12대가 이스라엘 오브다 기지에, 공중급유기 14대가 벤구리온 공항에 전개. 바레인의 5함대 사령부는 인원을 100명 미만으로 감축.
3cb4390a571f9967:en:
2.25–26

아락치가 "역사적 합의가 손에 잡힌다"고 발언. 제네바 3차 협상에서 오만 측은 이란이 '농축 우라늄 재고 제로 + 전면 IAEA 검증'을 제안했다고 설명. 알부사이디: "가장 중요한 성과는 이란이 핵무기용 물질을 결코 갖지 않기로 한 것." 단, 월스트리트저널은 미국이 포르도·나탄즈·이스파한의 물리적 파괴와 농축 우라늄 전량 인도를 요구했다고 보도 — 두 설명이 충돌.
d4fb3ab9627f9238:en:
